title: Intermittent negative invoice adjustments caused by late-joining streaming sessions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple hosted and dedicated customers reported unexpected negative invoice line-items (credits) that appeared after long-running streaming sessions completed. The credits correlate with sessions that joined an already-warm KV/prefix cache mid-stream and then triggered a delayed reconciliation job which retroactively adjusted token counts downward, producing net negative adjustments on invoices. This ticket captures triage notes, repro steps, mitigation, and a proposed permanent fix path.
impact_summary: High-severity customer escalations from finance teams; two enterprise customers paused billing due to unexplained credits and one CSAT-critical account escalated to support and SEs. Affected environments: hosted (primary), dedicated pools with autoscaler enabled; private not observed yet. Potential revenue impact and trust degradation if unresolved.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a long streaming chat session with an initial cold start (no KV cache entries)
2) Route a set of additional requests that warm a separate prefix using the same tenant within the same node group
3) Allow autoscaler to add capacity or migrate requests (simulated by toggling pool size in staging)
4) Complete streaming sessions and trigger post-session accounting job (run ledger reconciler)
5) Observe retroactive negative adjustments in accounting logs and ledger rollups
observed_logs: 2026-03-09T21:42:12Z accounting-service INFO reconcile: tenant=acct-842 tokens_before=1,648,213 tokens_after=1,622,487 delta=-25,726 source=session-reconciler job_id=rec-7201
streaming-node-77 WARN kvcache: joined-prefix-warmup tenant=acct-842 prefix=usr:session:kv size_delta=128kb
router DEBUG request-id=req-9a2: merged-session into pooled-queue node=node-77 routing-hint=kv-warmup
root_cause_hypothesis: The post-session reconciler applies a deduplication/merge that assumes all session prefixes were present at session start. When a prefix is populated mid-session (cache warm-up), token attribution is moved between in-memory transient accounting and persistent ledger entries. A race between the streaming node committing partial token tallies and the reconciler merging persistent artifacts causes the reconciler to subtract a duplicate set of tokens, producing net negative deltas.
mitigation: Temporarily disabled automatic retroactive ledger adjustments and set reconciler to emit warnings (non-destructive mode) for any negative-delta events. Support notified customers and created manual backfill procedures for affected invoices. Enabled increased sampling logs for streaming accounting path.
next_steps: 1) Add strong invariants to reconciler: never reduce an account's cumulative token total without cross-checking distributed op ids and last-applied timestamps
2) Introduce a fix that stamps per-session token increments with node-scoped sequence ids to make merges idempotent
3) Build an e2e staging test that simulates mid-session prefix warm-ups with autoscaler churn
4) Deploy reconciler in feature-flagged safe mode and run on a subset of tenants for 48 hours before full rollout
